newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp supervisors approve cost-cutting. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Krupp supervisors approve cost-cutting. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]

text.p: German steel maker Krupp Hoesch Stahl AG said on Wednesday its supervisory board approved a cost-cutting plan that would eliminate 2,200 of the company's 10,000 jobs. (Corrects from "plan that would lay off 2,200 of the company's 10,000 workers" to make clear that jobs lost through attrition.)
More than 1,000 workers had stopped work earlier on Wednesday to protest the plan, which also includes 660 million marks ($400.7 million) in investments to optimise production.
The supervisory board approved the plan with the support of members representing employees because it called for eliminating jobs through attrition or the sale of business units, Krupp said.

The plan also called for Krupp to install new thin band technology around the year 2000 that should reduce production costs significantly. Other investments would be aimed at cutting smleting and metalurgy costs, the company said.
"Extraordinary steps are necessary to avoid being caught up by losses," said Krupp chief Gerhard Cromme.
Krupp aimed to become the cost leader among European steel suppliers, the company said.
